$comment: The dependency contract for the Kubermatic frontend stack.
Three categories, because they behave differently and conflating them breaks things:
singletons — carry React context or hook identity. A second copy in one app is an
invalid-hook-call or a form that cannot see its own provider. These stay
peerDependencies everywhere; what is centralised is the VERSION, applied by each
product as `overrides`. npm and pnpm cannot inherit overrides from a dependency,
so this file has to be written into each product's package.json — that is what
`kubermatic-config check --fix` does, and what the CI check enforces.
owned — no cross-boundary identity requirement, so ui-kit/ui-patterns take them as
direct dependencies and products get them transitively. A product declaring one
of these is a drift bug: `check` fails on it.
toolchain — build-time only, never a runtime import, so it cannot be vendored
through a runtime package. Shipped as the configs in this package plus the
Every version here is one this repo installs and its CI verifies. Versions that
cannot be grounded that way live in `pending` and make `check` report an unresolved
decision rather than silently bless a guess.

pending.@tanstack/react-query: Drifts across products. No version is installed in this repo, so there is nothing here to verify one against. Pin when ui-patterns takes a data-fetching dependency, or when a product owner picks the target.
pending.@tanstack/react-router: Used by KubeV and KubeLB, not by KDP, and not installed here. Blocked behind the Tier 2 router adapter — pinning a router version before deciding whether ui-patterns may reference one at all would prejudge that.
pending.zustand: Drifts across products. Not installed here.
pending.typescript@6: Products split ~5.9.3 vs ~6.0.3. `toolchain.typescript` holds 5.9.3 because that is the compiler this repo builds and typechecks under; 6.x is a major with real breakage and needs a migration, not a manifest edit.
